output: ONYX is a locally hosted coding agent: it runs on your machine with no subscription, and your code never leaves the device unless you point it at your own local model server. You train it by feeding it training data (JSONL packs), and it keeps that knowledge in ~/.onyx/knowledge.json so every later session can use it.

input: how do i train onyx on my own data?
output:
Put your records in a JSONL file and run:

```
onyx train training.jsonl
```

Inside the app you can do the same with `/train training.jsonl`. The run prints how many records were parsed and saved, then the knowledge is available immediately and after restarts. `--replace` rebuilds the knowledge from scratch instead of adding to it.

input: what format does onyx training data use?
output: One JSON object per line. A question/answer record needs `input` and `output`; a reference record needs `kind`:"doc" plus `title` and `text`. Optional fields: `id`, `tags`, `source`. basetrainer.txt holds the full spec and a prompt that makes any AI produce a pack for you.

input: can onyx answer with a real model instead of just showing records?
output:
Yes. Point it at any OpenAI-compatible server running on your machine:

```
/model http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 llama3.1:8b
```

Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM all work. The setting is saved in ~/.onyx/config.json, and the matching records are passed to the model as ground truth. Without a model, ONYX answers by showing the best-matching trained records.

input: where does onyx store what it learned?
output: In ~/.onyx/knowledge.json (override the folder with the ONYX_HOME environment variable). Settings live next to it in ~/.onyx/config.json. `onyx knowledge` prints the path, size, training runs and sources; `onyx forget --yes` deletes the trained knowledge while keeping your settings.

title: ONYX command cheat sheet
text: Start the app: `onyx`. Train: `onyx train path/to/data.jsonl`. One-shot question: `onyx ask "how do i undo a commit?"`. Inspect: `onyx knowledge`. Clear: `onyx forget --yes`. Version: `onyx version`. Inside the app: /train, /knowledge, /status, /model, /forget, /clear, /exit.

title: Using ONYX
text: A starter pack about ONYX itself: what it is, how training works, the training-data format, connecting a local model, where knowledge is stored, and the command cheat sheet.
